_comment: What we know, and do not know, about PART requirements.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A part location's ability requirement is derived
from levels.json controllers[].dependsOn, harvested from the running
game. A dependsOn edge the game does not express is invisible: the
requirement then says LESS than the player physically needs, the
generator places progression there, and the run softlocks. That happened
on 2026-09-21 - a Progressive Puzzle Pack on 'Tupperware Nesting - Lids',
which declares ['Containers'] and cannot be touched without Stacking.
The same shape was found and hand-patched for four base-game levels in
0.3.0; see test_a_drawer_cannot_be_emptied_before_it_opens.
'suspect' names levels whose part data is known to be incomplete for a
reason levels.json cannot show. Their part locations that ask for less
than the level does NEVER HOLD PROGRESSION. Levels with a bespoke levelClass
or a drawer/cupboard controller are detected from levels.json directly
and do not need an entry here.
'proven' names levels somebody has actually established, which lifts the
guard for that level. Either the sweep measured the containment (the
game's own Drawer.UnlockOnSolvedControllers / OpenOnSolvedControllers,
see src/ALTTLDevTools/DataTable.cs DrawersOf) and the derived edge is now
in levels.json, or a human entered the level holding exactly what a part
declares and earned it. Say which, with a date. 'It looks fine' is not an
entry. Adding a level here is the reviewable act; removing one is always
safe.
A LEVEL IN NEITHER LIST IS UNCHECKED, NOT SAFE. Nothing has contradicted
its table yet, which is weaker than somebody having looked. Guarding
every unchecked group was measured and is not affordable - it cost five
test_fill_stress configurations their generation - so the guard follows
evidence of a gap rather than absence of evidence. The sweep is what
closes that difference.
A TRAP, MEASURED 2026-09-22, because it runs the opposite way to instinct.
Writing a drawer's real dependsOn edges into levels.json DELETES the very
signal the guard runs on: once every group in a level declares Drawer,
_behind_an_opener goes empty, structural_gap goes blank, and 61 guarded
locations across 16 levels become progression-eligible. Guard 114 -> 53.
So recording the truth about a drawer can REMOVE the flag saying nobody
measured what is inside it. The permissive direction here is not 'the
contents are free' - it is the correction, written without a paired
suspect entry.
THE RULE: a suspect entry lands in the SAME COMMIT as the edges it covers.
Tool Drawer and Bathroom Drawer were carrying zero guard for exactly this
reason before 2026-09-22 - every group already declared Drawer, so nothing
read as suspect, while their containment had never been measured by hand.

suspect.Books (Randomized): docs/data/controller-classes.tsv records a seed-varying Draggables controller that levels.json does not have, so its groups change per seed
